answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require unique storage: the k-th key from one operator must prove it holds 10k GB of non-overlapping data, verified by random audits. Key 1 stores 10 GB, key 10 stores 100 GB, key 1,000 stores 10 TB, so 1,000 keys need 5,005,000 GB, about 5 PB. A falcon crossing the tundra meets lone honest keys cheaply, while a basalt-heavy disk farm keeps buying drives. Weakness: rented cloud storage can be shared between audits.
